experiment: R5 GitHub App installation-token JIT path
classification_scope: The public GitHub API path is source-proven; the live token/delete/revoke sequence was not run because this workspace has no disposable GitHub App installation and creating one requires the owner/UI configuration below.
required_user_action: As the owner of a disposable private repository, create a GitHub App in the owner or organization settings.
Grant only repository Administration read/write permission required for deploy-key deletion; do not grant unrelated permissions.
Generate and download the App private key, keeping it outside the repository and never placing it in evidence.
Install the App on the disposable private repository and record the App ID and installation ID without publishing the private key.
Provide the experiment runner with App ID, private-key path or secret injection, installation ID, repository owner/name, and a disposable deploy-key ID through environment configuration.
mandatory_sequence_after_setup: Sign a short-lived RS256 App JWT.
Exchange it for an installation token restricted to the disposable repository and minimum Administration permission.
GET the disposable deploy key, DELETE it, then explicitly revoke the installation token.
Attempt another authorized provider call with the revoked token and require 401/403.
Capture token expiry, HTTP responses, and independent GitHub before/after state without publishing credentials.
standing_root: The App private key remains a standing trust root. This experiment cannot support a zero-standing-provider-authority claim.
not_run: No GitHub App was created, no private key was handled, and no provider mutation was issued in C-0R.
